instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Ask Around the Missing Detail
cards.instruction: Find one hidden fact by asking about everything surrounding it and never naming it directly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave that second cup where it is. Was the tea in it strong or weak?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why don't you just ask who visited while you were out?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll choose the questions. Start with the tea, then tell me whether the sugar bowl was used.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Strong, no sugar. That's how half our friends drink it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll narrow it down. Did you bring out the biscuits, or did the bowl of mints have to come down from the shelf?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the extra dinner plate for a moment. Tell me what time the kitchen light went off.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could just ask who came over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll do this in order. Start with the time, and whether supper ended before the last bus.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: After it. We talked for hours, then I called a taxi.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Now give me the taxi destination, just the street. We can leave names until I've finished with the evening.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Recruit Them Twice
cards.instruction: Recruit them to your side, then reveal that the side, goal, or conflict is not what it first appeared to be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come and help me clear the committee cupboard. Start with the minutes; I'll tell you what we're keeping.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sure. Shall I throw out the old ones?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. Those show three years of postponed repairs. You'll read the dates while I ask for a new committee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I agreed to clear a cupboard, not help you remove people.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose now: leave me the minutes and stay out of the vote, or stand beside me and read them. We're deciding what this committee has been keeping shut.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stand with me at the club meeting. We're going to save the garden.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Absolutely. Who's trying to build on it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We are. Our extension plan puts the kitchen there. I'll withdraw my signature first; you follow me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So we're opposing the plan we persuaded everyone to support?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. You can explain why we sold it to them, and I'll explain what we missed. Are you beside me for that, or shall I leave room for you on the other side?

cards.title: Make the Second Step First
cards.instruction: Get them to accept a small consequence that makes the larger risky action feel already underway.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put down the climbing-course deposit. We can discuss the cliff after we've secured the places.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't agreed to climb. Is the deposit refundable?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only if we attend the first lesson. Book us both; I'll make sure we're there to ask for it back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So once I've paid, you can use getting my money back to get me to the lesson.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Put your name down first, then mine. Tomorrow I'll pick you up for the refund, and we can meet the instructor while we're waiting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell the committee we're considering a festival bid. Send that sentence today; leave the decision to me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We haven't agreed to bid. Why announce it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So they'll hold the date. Once our name is beside it, we can discuss whether to let it go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And if they tell everyone we're doing it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then forward that announcement to me before you correct it. I'll show you who is already expecting us, and we'll decide which of them you want to disappoint.

cards.title: Let the Callback Claim Credit
cards.instruction: Get recognition by returning to an early overlooked contribution when its importance becomes undeniable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Remember my suggestion to put the spare key under the flowerpot?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I called it unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. And now we're locked out beside a very useful flowerpot.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. Good idea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say whose idea while you lift it. The pot can't accept all the credit.

cards.title: Make the Choice Rewrite the Past
cards.instruction: Make them choose between options whose consequences reinterpret an earlier promise, refusal, or agreement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Choose the overseas job or running this shop with me. I'm going to know what your 'we'll build something' promised.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said that before the job offer arrived.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then decide what survives the offer. Stay, and I'll call it a promise to work beside me. Go, and I'll call it encouragement you gave me to work alone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're turning a job into a goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose what you're saying goodbye to. I'll keep the shop either way, but I'm not keeping your name on our plan while you decide what it meant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put my spare key on the table or keep it. I'm settling what you meant last week by 'take some space.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant one quiet evening, not a new arrangement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then keep it, and I'll treat that evening as over. You can come round as before.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And if I give it back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll treat the quiet evening as the start of visiting by invitation. Put it here, and next time you ask before you come.
